chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about the charity of Fitra, 'Can I give it to other than the people of Wilayah, from the poor ones of my neighbours?' He said: 'Yes. The neighbour is more rightful with it, due to the place (status) well known'.

key_terms.لِمَكَانِ الشُّهْرَةِ: Due to the place/status well known

ai.seo_question: Can I give Zakat al-Fitr to non-Shia neighbours?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the preferential right of neighbours to Zakat al-Fitr is based on their established proximity and public recognition (shuhra), rather than religious affiliation. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the social bond of neighbourliness holds independent merit, allowing the charity to be distributed to non-Shia poor neighbours while still prioritizing them over distant relatives or others. This highlights the universal social welfare aspect of Fitra within the Shia tradition.
